package_info.why_malicious: The Slinger HTTP server contains a directory traversal vulnerability caused by improper ordering of input sanitization and URI decoding. This flaw allows attackers to craft network requests that access arbitrary files or execute arbitrary code outside the intended web root or CGI directories, resulting in unauthorized file disclosure and potential remote code execution.

execution_context.file_location: Slinger HTTP server request handler (binary/firmware code)

malicious_snippets.code_language: HTTP (network protocol, interpreted by C/C++ server code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the server receives a crafted HTTP GET request containing an encoded directory traversal sequence (/.%2e/), decodes the URI after sanitization, accesses a file outside the intended web root, and returns its contents to the requester, resulting in unauthorized file disclosure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it allows attackers to bypass directory restrictions by encoding traversal sequences, enabling access to sensitive files outside the web root.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would strictly prevent access to files outside the web root, even if traversal sequences are encoded. Here, the improper order of URI decoding and sanitization allows traversal to succeed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would only serve files within the web root, with all traversal attempts—encoded or not—blocked by the server.
key_indicators: Decoding of URI after input sanitization
Presence of encoded traversal sequences (/.%2e/ or similar) in HTTP requests
File access outside the designated web root directory
HTTP responses containing contents of sensitive or non-web-root files

execution_context.trigger: runtime (CGI script execution via HTTP request)
execution_context.file_location: Slinger HTTP server CGI handler (binary/firmware code)

malicious_snippets.code_language: HTTP (network protocol, interpreted by C/C++ server code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the server receives a crafted HTTP GET request targeting the CGI handler, decodes multiple encoded traversal and path separator sequences in the script path, escapes the CGI directory, and executes an arbitrary system binary (/usr/sbin/logger) with attacker-controlled parameters, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it enables attackers to execute arbitrary system commands by escaping the CGI directory using encoded traversal and path separators, violating directory isolation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict CGI execution to approved scripts within the CGI directory, blocking any traversal or encoded path manipulation. Here, the server fails to enforce these restrictions, allowing execution of system binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would only execute CGI scripts located within the designated CGI directory, with no possibility to reference or execute binaries outside this directory.
key_indicators: Encoded traversal and path separators (%2e, %2f) in CGI script path
CGI handler executing binaries outside the CGI directory
Attacker-controlled parameters passed to system binaries
HTTP requests invoking system-level executables via CGI

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request with encoded directory traversal sequences to the Slinger server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Unauthorized file disclosure from outside the web root.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request to the CGI handler with encoded traversal and path separators, escaping the CGI directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote execution of arbitrary system binaries with attacker-controlled parameters.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP requests containing encoded directory traversal sequences such as /.%2e/ or %2e%2e%2f in the URI path
Access attempts to files outside the web root or CGI directory by the HTTP server process
Execution of system binaries via CGI handler with encoded traversal in the script path
file_indicators: HTTP access attempts to sensitive files (e.g., /private/secret.txt) using encoded traversal sequences
CGI handler invoked with script paths containing encoded traversal (e.g., /cgi-bin/%2e%2e%2f.../usr/sbin/logger)
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with %2e (.) and %2f (/) in the URI path, especially in locations not expected for normal web traffic
Unusual GET requests targeting the CGI handler with encoded traversal and system binary paths
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP server logs for requests containing encoded directory traversal sequences (such as /.%2e/, %2e%2e%2f, or similar patterns) and attempts to access files or execute binaries outside the designated web root or CGI directories. Set alerts for any CGI execution requests where the script path includes encoded traversal or references to system binaries. Use file access monitoring to detect unauthorized reads or executions initiated by the HTTP server process, and correlate with suspicious network requests to identify exploitation attempts.
